founder.title: The founder's hall, on the summit
founder.sub: Where ranks are certified. Plain at the centre, crowded with witnesses at the edge.
items: the founder's cell: mat, desk, his unfinished BARs
founder.size: 30 m by 20 m, 7.5 m to the beam
labels_extra: the eight-trigram floor: you kneel at its centre
doors: great doors from the great court
doors to the Heaven altar, open sky
does: You walk in at the great doors with your witnesses on the benches behind you.
You kneel at the centre of the trigram floor; the Elder who taught you stands at your side.
The founder reads your BAR aloud from the plain mat, then hangs your tablet on the lineage wall.
The gold seams on his own tablets are the ranks he only squeaked through. He shows you them.
founder.bend: The founder's own plan, unbent: red plaster, teal and gold beam, nothing he did not need.

elder.title: The Shaman Elder's house, at the cave mouth
elder.sub: The founder's plan bent by one Elder: low, earthen, the mountain itself for a back wall.
items: listening stone in the cave niche
herb room: drying rack, water jar
tea kettle on the low table
rain porch and the shoe step
elder.size: 14 m by 10 m, 3.2 m to the beam; the cave goes 1.2 m deeper
does: You leave your shoes on the step and duck in under the one teal beam the founder insisted on.
The Elder sits at the hearth; your team sits on the cushions. Tea first, then the Wake Up scan.
The ember jars on the shelf are spirits the Elder has cleaned up. One glows when you are near.
The listening stone is where the Elder sits alone. You are not asked in until Practitioner.
elder.bend: Founder's standard kept: the teal beam, the court's red gate. Elder's bend: earth walls, cave, smoke.

lieutenant.title: A lieutenant's room: Virelune, in the Shaman's court
lieutenant.sub: One of thirty. Your team's mentor lives here; the room is the nation, the walls are the founder's.
items: three cubbies: your team's BAR folders
drill board: the team's wax-on marks
lieutenant.size: 5.5 m by 4.5 m, 2.8 m to the trellis
does: Your mentor's door is the one with a vine over it. You knock; you are let in to sit.
Your team's three folders are in the cubbies. The mentor reads your last BAR at the desk.
The drill board shows the team's wax-on marks for the five basic moves, chalked by hand.
The other four lieutenants' rooms in this court share the walls and differ in everything else.
lieutenant.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, teal beam, the same door. Nation's dress: plants, seeds, a vine roof.

elder-challenger.title: The Challenger Elder's house, at the forge
elder-challenger.sub: The founder's plan bent by one Elder: one wall is a rail over the drop, and the floor is for fighting on.
elder-challenger.bend: Founder's standard kept: the teal beam, the south door. Elder's bend: a forge, a sand floor, an open side.
items: rack of staves and wooden swords
bench for whoever waits to be tested
does: The east wall stops at your waist. Past the rail the cliff drops into the cloud sea.
The Elder fights you on the sand before saying a word. How you fall is the first lesson.
Strike the gong and the Elder must answer a challenge. Students rarely strike it twice.
The forge mends the court's tools, and its heat is the Elder's: you work beside it, not away from it.
elder-challenger.size: 14 m by 10 m, 3.6 m to the beam

elder-regent.title: The Regent Elder's house, the hall of records
elder-regent.sub: The founder's plan bent by one Elder: every wall is shelving, and the middle of the floor is still water.
elder-regent.bend: Founder's standard kept: red plaster, the teal beam. Elder's bend: records to the roof, a basin, a screen.
items: record shelves, every rank since the founding
reading desk and the rank register
paper screen before the sleeping alcove
does: Your name is already on a shelf. The Regent finds it without looking.
The register on the desk is where a rank becomes true. The Elder writes it; the founder signs it.
Nobody walks through the basin. You walk round it, and you see yourself in it on the way.
The copyists are students working off a debt. The water clock tells them when they may stop.
elder-regent.size: 14 m by 10 m, 3.4 m to the beam

elder-architect.title: The Architect Elder's house, beside the timber yard
elder-architect.sub: The founder's plan bent by one Elder: tall enough for a loft, and the sect itself on a table in the middle.
elder-architect.bend: Founder's standard kept: red plaster, the teal beam. Elder's bend: a loft, timber, the sect in miniature.
items: drafting table, tilted to the light
the sect in miniature, every court
tool wall: squares, chisels, the plumb bob
the Elder's mat, up in the loft
does: The model on the table is the sect, every court to scale. Your bunk is on it, as a pin.
The Architect asks what you would build, then hands you a chisel and a joint to finish first.
The loft is the only room in the sect with a ladder. The Elder sleeps above the work.
Beams in the stack are seasoning for halls that are not drawn yet. Some have your team's mark.
elder-architect.size: 14 m by 10 m, 4.4 m to the beam

elder-diplomat.title: The Diplomat Elder's house, the tea room and guest rooms
elder-diplomat.sub: The founder's plan bent by one Elder: a room for sitting in a circle, and beds for whoever arrives.
elder-diplomat.bend: Founder's standard kept: red plaster, the teal beam. Elder's bend: a garden window, screens, guest rooms.
items: six cushions, one for each face
paper screens to the guest rooms
the Elder's mat, by the door
does: The Diplomat sleeps by the door, so whoever arrives in the night is met by a person, not a latch.
Six cushions round the tea table, one for each Elder. When they meet, they meet here.
The garden window is a whole wall open at sitting height. Tea is poured looking at the garden.
The guest rooms are for visitors from the settlements. You may be asked to give up your bunk for one.
elder-diplomat.size: 14 m by 10 m, 3.2 m to the beam

elder-sage.title: The Sage Elder's library cave, on the crag
elder-sage.sub: The founder's plan bent furthest: half cave, one seat, a window over the cloud sea, and books in the rock.
elder-sage.bend: Founder's standard kept: the teal beam, the red door. Elder's bend: the rock for a wall, the sea for a view.
items: scroll niches cut into the rock
the one seat, facing the window
a pot of tea gone cold
the Elder's mat, in a niche
oil lamp on the rock shelf
does: There is no yard and no gate. The path to the door bends three times, and the door is off-centre.
One seat, and the Sage is in it. You stand. Most students leave before being spoken to.
The window is the whole south wall above the sill: cloud sea, the summit, and the road you came by.
The scrolls are not catalogued. The Sage says the finding is the reading.
elder-sage.size: 10 m by 8 m, 3.0 m to the beam

lt-argyra.title: A lieutenant's room: Argyra
lt-argyra.sub: One of thirty. The Argyra lieutenant teaches the Elder's practice the metal way; the walls are the founder's.
items: three cubbies: your team's BAR folders
whetstone bench and the polished blades
drill board: the team's wax-on marks
a bronze mirror, the Argyra shrine
lt-argyra.size: 5.5 m by 4.5 m, 2.8 m to the trellis
does: Your mentor's door has a bronze plate on it. Everything in the room is sharpened or polished.
Your team's three folders are in the cubbies. The mentor reads your last BAR at the desk.
The drill board shows the team's wax-on marks for the five basic moves, chalked by hand.
The other four lieutenants' rooms in this court share the walls and differ in everything else.
lt-argyra.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, teal beam, the same door. Nation's dress: whetstone bench and the polished blades, a bronze mirror.

lt-lamenth.title: A lieutenant's room: Lamenth
lt-lamenth.sub: One of thirty. The Lamenth lieutenant teaches the Elder's practice the water way; the walls are the founder's.
items: three cubbies: your team's BAR folders
basin stand and the tide chart
drill board: the team's wax-on marks
a still bowl of water, the Lamenth shrine
lt-lamenth.size: 5.5 m by 4.5 m, 2.8 m to the trellis
does: Your mentor's door has a blue cloth over it. A basin stands by the window, and nothing is hurried.
Your team's three folders are in the cubbies. The mentor reads your last BAR at the desk.
The drill board shows the team's wax-on marks for the five basic moves, chalked by hand.
The other four lieutenants' rooms in this court share the walls and differ in everything else.
lt-lamenth.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, teal beam, the same door. Nation's dress: basin stand and the tide chart, a still bowl of water.

lt-pyrakanth.title: A lieutenant's room: Pyrakanth
lt-pyrakanth.sub: One of thirty. The Pyrakanth lieutenant teaches the Elder's practice the fire way; the walls are the founder's.
items: three cubbies: your team's BAR folders
drill board: the team's wax-on marks
the ember lamp, the Pyrakanth shrine
lt-pyrakanth.size: 5.5 m by 4.5 m, 2.8 m to the trellis
does: Your mentor's door is scorched round the frame. The brazier is always lit, even in summer.
Your team's three folders are in the cubbies. The mentor reads your last BAR at the desk.
The drill board shows the team's wax-on marks for the five basic moves, chalked by hand.
The other four lieutenants' rooms in this court share the walls and differ in everything else.
lt-pyrakanth.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, teal beam, the same door. Nation's dress: brazier and the drill candles, the ember lamp.

lt-meridia.title: A lieutenant's room: Meridia
lt-meridia.sub: One of thirty. The Meridia lieutenant teaches the Elder's practice the earth way; the walls are the founder's.
items: three cubbies: your team's BAR folders
drill board: the team's wax-on marks
a standing stone, the Meridia shrine
lt-meridia.size: 5.5 m by 4.5 m, 2.8 m to the trellis
does: Your mentor's door is propped with a stone. The floor is beaten earth, swept twice a day.
Your team's three folders are in the cubbies. The mentor reads your last BAR at the desk.
The drill board shows the team's wax-on marks for the five basic moves, chalked by hand.
The other four lieutenants' rooms in this court share the walls and differ in everything else.
lt-meridia.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, teal beam, the same door. Nation's dress: clay jars of seed grain, a standing stone.

dojo.title: The dojo
dojo.sub: Where teams spar. The floor is straw mats, and the Root circle in the middle is where you learn to stand.
dojo.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, the teal beam, the founder's tablet over the floor. Its own: a drum and racks.
items: the founder's tablet: stand where you are
rack of wooden swords and spears
drill board: the five basic moves, each team's wax-on marks
bench for the team that waits its turn
bench for the team that waits its turn
does: The Root circle is the first drill. Your teammate pushes; you learn to stay where you stand.
Teams spar in threes on the mats. The team that waits sits on the bench by the door and watches.
Every move done clean earns a chalk mark on the drill board. Wax-on: the same move until it is yours.
The founder's tablet over the floor says one thing: stand where you are.
dojo.size: 18 m by 14 m, 5.0 m to the beam

refectory.title: The refectory
refectory.sub: Where the sect eats. Each low table seats one team of three, and this is where you meet yours.
refectory.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, the teal beam. Its own: a kitchen hearth, and the founder's empty seat.
items: the head table, and the founder's seat kept empty
the founder's cushion, never sat on
chore board: who carries water, who cooks
does: Your team is the two at the table with the empty stool. You sit, and the three of you are a team.
Teams eat together and clear together. The chore board by the door says whose day it is.
The head table has one cushion nobody sits on. It is the founder's, kept for when the founder comes home.
The kitchen fire never goes out. Anyone may ask the cook for tea after the bell.
refectory.size: 24 m by 10 m, 4.4 m to the beam

arrival-hall.title: The arrival hall
arrival-hall.sub: Twelve bunks for exiles in their first nights. The Steward senior keeps the register at the door.
arrival-hall.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, the teal beam. Its own: two tiers of bunks, a register, a screen.
items: the Steward's desk and the arrivals register
notice of the first week: bell, water, class
does: The Steward writes your name in the register, then hands you the bunk with the red blanket.
Twelve bunks, two tiers. Exiles sleep here until their team takes them to a house in the rows.
The notice on the wall says the whole first week: the bell, the water, the first class.
Nobody asks why you were exiled. The register has a column for it, and it is blank.
arrival-hall.size: 16 m by 8 m, 4.0 m to the beam

team-1.title: A team house: house 1
team-1.sub: One of eight in the exiles' rows. A team of three sleeps, eats breakfast and argues here.
team-1.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, the teal beam, the same door in every house. Its own: the team's mark.
items: peg rail and three practice robes
the team's mark, painted on the north wall
does: Another team's house. The door is open if they are home; you knock anyway.
Their mark on the wall is older than yours. Ask them what it means.
team-1.size: 6 m by 5 m, 3.0 m to the beam

team-3.title: A team house: yours, house 3
team-3.sub: Your team's house: three mats, one low table, and the lantern lit at your door.
team-3.bend: Founder's standard: red plaster, the teal beam, the same door in every house. Its own: the team's mark.
items: peg rail and three practice robes
the team's mark, painted on the north wall
does: The lantern at your door is lit because you are home. Every team lights its own.
Three mats, three trunks, one table. What you keep here is what you carried up the mountain.
The team's mark on the wall is painted the night the team forms. Yours is new gold.
Breakfast is at the low table before the bell. It is where the team decides who leads the day.
team-3.size: 6 m by 5 m, 3.0 m to the beam
